name: Black and lime
description: White forward fuselage with a large black lower-case 'flair' over the forward cabin. A black band runs along the lower fuselage from just behind the nose; behind the wing a swoosh sweeps down from the crown to the belly, edged with a lime and a purple pinstripe, and everything aft of it is black. Black fin with a big lime disc at its foot, running down over the tail. Lime engines with bare lips, lime winglets.

titles.style: 'flair' in a heavy, slightly condensed lower-case sans, tall ascenders, set tight; across the windows over the forward cabin, from just behind the forward door to the engine's inlet.

logos.description: Small Canadian flag behind the registration, over the rear windows.

notes: Measured on C-FFFX (737-8, left side, LAX, 2023-11-06); still the scheme on C-FLKA in July 2026. The title runs x 0.205-0.396 with its baseline at y -0.35 (below the windows) and its ascenders at y 0.64, about 2.7 m tall; lower case at 0.63 of that. The swoosh reaches the crown at about x 0.56 (hidden by the wing; a little of it shows above the wing root), the pinstripes about 0.35 m wide each. White lettering runs along the black belly (seen upside down from below; not readable in these photos, so not drawn). Some leased 737-8s fly a simpler variant (C-FLUJ, LAX 2023-09-12): an all-white body with the same 'flair', the black fin with its lime disc, white engines and blue winglets; not drawn. The 'from' year is left out: no dated source for the scheme's introduction in hand.
history: New in the LAX round (2026-11-20); Flair had no scheme here before.
